text: Tell me about a time you changed a technical plan because of what you learned about users' needs.
assesses: Whether the candidate grounds engineering decisions in real user impact.
strongSignals: Gathered direct evidence from users, support tickets or data
Changed course even at personal or schedule cost
Can quantify the outcome for users
followUps: How did you get that user signal?
What did you give up to make the change?
How did you know it worked?

text: Describe a bug or incident you caused that affected customers. What happened and what did you change afterwards?
assesses: Accountability, learning and systemic fixes after mistakes.
strongSignals: Owns the mistake plainly without deflecting
followUps: How was it detected?
What did the post-mortem conclude?
What would have caught it earlier?

text: Tell me about a time you had to deliver something important under a tight deadline. How did you decide what to cut?
assesses: Prioritisation and focus without sacrificing critical quality.
redFlags: Cut testing on critical paths silently
followUps: What did you refuse to cut and why?
What happened to the deferred work?
Would you do it the same way again?

text: Give an example of a problem outside your team's remit that you took responsibility for fixing.
strongSignals: Drove it to a durable resolution
followUps: Why did you think it was yours to fix?
How did the owning team react?
What was the long-term outcome?

text: Tell me about a significant technical disagreement with a peer or another team. How was it resolved?
assesses: Ability to disagree productively and egolessly.
strongSignals: Sought to understand the other view first
Used data or prototypes to decide
Committed fully once decided, even if overruled
followUps: What was the strongest point of their argument?
What would have changed your mind?
How is the relationship now?

text: Describe a design or API decision you made with long-term consequences. How did you weigh short-term speed against long-term cost?
assesses: Long-term thinking about API and system design.
strongSignals: Made the decision reversible where possible
followUps: What would it cost to change now?
Who else did you consult?
Looking back, was it right?

text: Tell me about someone you helped grow significantly as an engineer.
assesses: Investment in others and raising the bar.
followUps: What feedback was hardest to give?
How did you adjust when it wasn't working?
Where are they now?

text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical and how you found out.
assesses: Curiosity, humility and openness to evidence.
strongSignals: Specific belief and evidence that changed it
followUps: Who pointed it out?
What did you do differently afterwards?
How do you test your assumptions now?

text: Describe the most detail-sensitive system you've worked on (e.g. money, data integrity). How did you ensure correctness?
strongSignals: Monitoring for correctness not only uptime
followUps: What invariant did you monitor?
What was the scariest edge case?
How did you roll out changes?

text: Tell me about a time you had to align several teams on a direction you didn't have authority to mandate.
assesses: Influence without authority across an organisation.
followUps: Who was hardest to convince and why?
What did you compromise on?
How did you measure adoption?
